0.0.n: Used to open the greeting and get the viewer's attention, rather than answer a question.

0.2.n: Combines with ございます to make a polite morning greeting.

0.3.n: This is the stem of ござる; together with ます, it makes おはよう polite.

0.4.n: Attaches to ござい to complete the polite greeting.

0.6.n: A person's name, written in katakana here.

0.7.n: A polite sentence ending; the speaker leaves out the understood subject, I.

1.0.n: Sets the time for the plan being described.

1.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic: what the speaker will do today.

1.2.n: Describes how regularly Yui puts in effort.

1.3.n: 頑張って + くれている contracts to 頑張ってくれてる, expressing ongoing effort that benefits the speaker or family.

1.4.n: A person's name; the subtitle reads ゆい, despite the supplied dictionary label ゆう.

1.5.n: Marks Yui as the person being allowed or helped to refresh herself.

1.6.n: させる adds the idea of making or letting someone do something; here, it means giving Yui a break.

1.7.n: After a verb, ために expresses the purpose of an action.

1.8.n: Completes ために, linking Yui's refreshment to the plan that follows.

2.0.n: This subtitle chunk combines 一日, a day's duration, with 外, outside; it is not a single word.

2.1.n: Marks 外 as the destination of going.

2.2.n: The て-form of 行く connects to おいで in a friendly instruction to go out and return.

2.3.n: After 行って, this gives a familiar, encouraging instruction rather than a formal command.

2.4.n: Links the preceding instruction to こと, though this wording is unusual and may reflect a subtitle error.

2.5.n: Refers to the preceding instruction as a situation or arrangement; the surrounding subtitle wording is irregular.

2.6.n: Connects that arrangement to the solo-parenting day described next.

3.0.n: Short for ワンオペレーション; here it describes caring for a child without another adult's help.

3.1.n: The English word is mixed into Japanese to label the day's theme casually.

3.2.n: Marks the resulting situation with なる: becoming a solo-parenting day.

3.3.n: The polite form of なる, describing how the day will turn out.

3.5.n: A personal pronoun commonly used by male speakers; here it identifies who will handle parenting alone.

3.6.n: Marks 僕 as the subject, added afterward to clarify that he is the solo parent.

4.0.n: Used with の to describe this as their first such experience.

4.1.n: Links 初めて to the following description, making it their first time alone together.

4.2.n: っきり emphasizes that no one else is there.

4.3.n: Links 二人っきり to 時間, describing time spent with only two people present.

4.4.n: Refers to a period spent together, not a clock reading.

4.5.n: Politely completes the description of their time together.

4.7.n: Added after the main statement to specify when this first experience happens.

4.8.n: Marks 今日 as the topic, placed at the end as a conversational afterthought.

5.0.n: Connects the previous situation to the speaker's decision to film.

5.1.n: Specifies when the filming will take place.

5.2.n: Makes 今日 the topic of the filming plan.

5.3.n: Points back to the solo-parenting time he has just described.

5.4.n: Refers to what the experience looks like as it unfolds.

5.5.n: Marks その様子 as the object of 撮る.

5.6.n: 撮って + いこう combines filming with moving forward; いこう expresses an intention or suggestion.

5.7.n: Combines with な to make かな, expressing gentle uncertainty about the plan.

5.8.n: Completes かな, giving the intention a tentative, conversational tone.

5.9.n: Marks the preceding thought as the content of 思います.

5.10.n: The polite form of 思う; here it softens the announcement of his plan.

6.0.n: Signals a transition from the introduction to the rest of the video.

6.1.n: Refers to the continuation of the video after this introduction.

6.2.n: Marks 続き as the object of an understood verb such as watch.

6.3.n: Invites viewers to watch; the long dash represents a stretched, cheerful final vowel.

0.tip: Japanese often leaves out I when the speaker introduces themselves with a name plus です.

1.lit: Today, to let Yui, who always works hard for us, refresh herself,
1.tip: The description 頑張ってくれてる comes before Yui's name, and くれる adds appreciation for her effort.

2.lit: With the arrangement of go outside for a day and come back,
2.tip: 行っておいで is a friendly send-off; のことで is unusual here and may be a subtitle error.

3.lit: It will become a solo-parenting DAY. I am the one.
3.tip: 僕が is added after the sentence to clarify who will be parenting alone.

4.lit: It is the first time of just the two of us, as for today.
4.tip: 二人っきり emphasizes being together with nobody else around.

5.lit: So today, that situation, I'll film as we go, I wonder, I think.
5.tip: かなと思います makes a plan sound softer and more tentative than a direct announcement.

6.tip: どうぞ invites an action without stating the verb when the context makes it clear.
